attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He is describing what others said, but the claim that they said it is his.

semantics.note: Keeps the named people, the phrase, the diminishing-returns idea and the 'last couple weeks' window. It is a dated observation about public statements.

contract.note: The contract reads this as a claim about the group, so not every named person has to say 'wall' word for word. That is a fair, ordinary reading of a loose sentence covering both the phrase and the idea. A strict per-person reading would make Andreessen only a partial match: he said 'ceiling', not 'wall'. A Nov 6 date fits a loose 'couple weeks'.

evidence.note: Verge report on the Nov 20, 2024 event. Wang used the wall framing ('Have we hit a wall? Yes and no') three days before the post.
The same Verge report describes diminishing returns and wide industry agreement on a scaling wall in November 2024, which supports 'many others'.
Nov 6, 2024 report of Andreessen saying models were hitting a ceiling and topping out, i.e. the diminishing-returns idea. He did not say 'wall'. The remarks were made on or before the report date.

reviews.rationale: Dated reports from inside the window show Wang using the wall framing on Nov 20 and Andreessen describing a capability ceiling and topping out around Nov 6. The Verge reports that industry leaders widely agreed on a scaling wall. The claim holds on the contract's fair group reading. The only weak point is that Andreessen said 'ceiling', not 'wall'. No counterevidence.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in the epilogue of his post.

semantics.note: The wording matches the source. But 'practically an entire field' trying to 'shout me down' is a sweeping, hyperbolic description of how he was treated, not a testable observation. It is better classed as rhetoric.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no measure for the share of a field that tried to silence someone, or for when the 'data were in'. The 2022 start of its target period is not stated by Marcus, but this does not change the outcome.

reviews.rationale: This is a sweeping characterization of the field's response to Marcus, with no threshold or observable act that records could test. 'Long before the data were in' turns on a disputed judgment. The packet has no evidence and none could settle it, so it is not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Reading 'on the assumption that I was wrong' as 'on the assumption that scaling would keep working' is reasonable, and 'little investment' fairly renders 'largely to the exclusion'. It is a firm historical claim.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary. It requires three parts: size, rationale, and concentration. The 2020–2024 period follows from his 'almost a half decade'.

evidence.note: Combined 2024 capex of the big four, well over $200B. This is total data-center and cloud capex, a different metric from investment in LLM scaling, so it is context on size only.
Wang said much AI investment rested on the belief that the scaling law would hold. This supports the rationale part only and says nothing on funding for alternatives.

reviews.rationale: The rationale part is consistent with Wang's statement. Size is only suggested, by total capex on a different metric. No data cover funding for non-LLM approaches, so 'largely to the exclusion' cannot be checked. Nothing contradicts the claim, but the packet does not establish all three required parts.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: It is a causal claim that resistance delayed science. Marcus points the delay at considering alternatives to LLMs, and the normalised 'slowed scientific progress in AI' is a little broader. This does not affect the outcome.

contract.note: The contract rightly notes that testing this needs an unobservable counterfactual: the pace of alternative research with less resistance. It treats the claim as untestable.

reviews.rationale: The claim that science was delayed depends on a counterfactual baseline that no record measures. The packet has no evidence, and part of the claim is a general maxim. Not adjudicable.
